Our Valley Glass team is proud to be more than just a business; we’re a neighbor you can always count on. How long does windshield replacement or repair take? Windshield repairs typically take about 30 minutes, while windshield replacement can take around 60-90 minutes. The exact time depends on the extent of the damage and the type of vehicle. After a replacement, it’s essential to allow time for the adhesive to be properly set, so plan for a total of about two hours for the entire process. How important is scheduling windshield repair? Scheduling windshield repair promptly is crucial because small chips and cracks can quickly spread, compromising your vehicle’s safety. A damaged windshield can affect visibility and the structural integrity of your car, especially in the event of a collision. Timely windshield repair can prevent more costly replacements down the road. When should I replace my home’s windows? Consider replacing your home’s windows if they are drafty, difficult to open, have visible damage, or have higher energy bills than usual. Older windows that have deteriorated frames or single-pane glass may not be energy efficient. Upgrading to modern, energy-efficient windows can improve comfort, reduce utility costs, and enhance your home’s curb appeal. What windows are best for my new construction home? The best windows for new construction homes are energy-efficient, durable, and suited to your climate. Consider options with double or triple glazing, low-E coatings, and insulated frames to reduce energy costs. Additionally, choose windows that complement your home’s architectural style and meet any specific needs, such as noise reduction or UV protection. What ballistic glass is best for my commercial property? The best ballistic glass for your commercial property depends on the level of protection needed. Options range from laminated glass with polycarbonate layers to bullet-resistant glass panels. Assess the threat level and consult with professionals to choose the right ballistic rating, ensuring the glass meets safety and security standards for your specific application. Enhancing Energy Efficiency As a homeowner, you spend plenty of time and money in an attempt to conserve energy, from upgrading your insulation to installing high-efficiency HVAC systems. While these energy-efficient features certainly help you save electricity and money in the long run, they can’t provide maximum benefits if your windows allow for excessive heat exchange. Old, poorly-installed, or low-quality windows let warm air escape outside during the winter and allow the summer heat inside your home during the summer. This means that you’ll have to run your heater or air conditioner all day, every day, to keep your home at a comfortable temperature. Not only is this not energy efficient, but it can cost a lot of money when your utility bill comes every month. Some of the most common issues our technicians service, when a window fails, include: A blown fuse could be the result of a window that remains stationary when the switch is pressed. The power window regulator may have a mechanical issue if the window jams or does not move when the motor is running.
